newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Horta says Gusmao should have won Peace Prize.
newsitem.headline: Horta says Gusmao should have won Peace Prize.

text.p: Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta, a spokesman for the East Timor resistance movement, said on Friday his jailed leader Xanana Gusmao should have won the award.

Ramos-Horta, who has led the international campaign against Indonesian rule in the former Portuguese colony, told Reuters in Sydney, Australia: "I would feel much happier if, instead of my name, his was selected."
Ramos-Horta, honoured jointly with East Timor bishop Carlos Belo, told Portugal's TSF radio he had pressed "my friends in Scandanavia that...they should also propose Xanana (Gusmao)."
He said: "I believe this prize will give joy to Xanana Gusmao, just as he congratulated me when I received previous awards.
"I hope this prize will give even greater prestige to the name of Xanana Gusmao, our true leader."
In a separate interview with the Portuguese news agency Lusa, Ramos-Horta said: "I think the prize should have been awarded also to Xanana Gusmao, a hero who deserves much more than any one of us."
He said he had been "profoundly surprised" by the award.
"This news shocked me and I didn't want to believe it when I first heard it," he said.
Horta's sentiments were echoed by former Portuguese president Mario Soares, who welcomed the joint award Belo and Ramos-Horta but said Gusmao should also be remembered.

Speaking to a news conference in Geneva, where he chairs the Independent World Commission on the Oceans, Soares said the prestigious award was a "great encouragement for the brave and courageous people of East Timor".
Gusmao has been in prison in Jakarta, Indonesia, since 1992 when he was captured by Indonesian security forces and sentenced to 20 years in jail.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975, just after Portugal pulled out, and annexed the territory a year later. The annexation has never been recognised by the United Nations.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee said Ramos-Horta and Belo had been awarded the prize for "their work toward a just and peaceful solution to the conflict in East Timor."
The committee said Ramos-Horta "has been the leading international spokesman for East Timor's cause since 1975 when Indonesia seized control of East Timor".
